entries.name: Deathblast
entries.notes: SHIPPED — id, kind and element-variant expansion kept verbatim per naming.v1.json idNamespaces.affixFamilies (g.on-death existingFamilies), and per ssot-affixes.md's own worked example citing `atom.deathblast.omni.t5` as a real (crafted-only-weighted) row, which is what confirms this family carries the element variant rather than being a single-row one. `roles` is the on-death column of ssot-affixes.md §4.3's role x group matrix (weight > 0 for head-protective, core-protective, jewel-major, jewel-minor, armament-primary), translated to core.v1.json's 15 ids: head-protective->head-guard, core-protective->core-guard, jewel-minor->jewel-minor-a and jewel-minor-b, jewel-major and armament-primary stay. Every entry in this file shares this identical roles list, same as the on-hit group's file does for its own column. `displayTemplate` mirrors `searing_strike`'s shape (bonus element damage) but on the corpse's cell instead of the hit target, which is the trigger swap the whole family is built on.

entries.name: Martyrdom
entries.displayTemplate: heal allies {value}% of max health when this dies
entries.notes: SHIPPED, id kept verbatim. No `element` param and no `variants` — a single-row family, the death-side mirror of how `lifesteal` carries no variant on the on-hit side. The trigger is the same `OnDeath` as `deathblast`; the two shipped families split the wearer's-own-death perspective into an offensive burst (`deathblast`) and a defensive ally-heal (`martyrdom`), exactly the O/S split atom-family-library.md §3.3 records for this pair.

entries.name: Summoner
entries.displayTemplate: {value}% chance to spawn a zombie where this fell
entries.notes: SHIPPED, id kept verbatim. `kindId: spawn.entity` with `params.kind: "zombie"` matches AtomKindRegistry's spawn.entity schema, which honours `x`/`hp`/`maxHp`/`mindControlled` only for `kind=zombie` — this family supplies none of those, the same restraint `volley` shows for its own `kind: "bullet"` row on the on-hit side. `powerBand: low` for the same reason `volley` sits at `low`: a spawn rider is a bigger swing than an additive number and is kept modest relative to the additive riders (`deathblast`, `martyrdom`) beside it. atom-family-library.md §4.2 calls this family's home domain the zombie/creep side, which the flavour and `nameWords` lean into without the schema needing a faction field to say so.

entries.name: Gardener
entries.displayTemplate: {value}% chance to spawn a plant where this fell
entries.notes: SHIPPED, id kept verbatim, and the one family in this file with a real worked citation: ssot-affixes.md's draw example resolves row 4 as `atom.gardener.t2` -> "spawn 1 plant OnDeath, 250 permille", confirming both the trigger and that the count/chance split is a generated magnitude, never authored here. `params.kind: "plant"` is the plant-side twin of `summoner`'s `kind: "zombie"`, the same pairing atom-family-library.md §3.5 and §4.2 draw between them. `tags: ["utility"]` rather than `["offensive"]` follows that same table's O/U split for the pair — a new plant on the board is board presence and tempo, not a direct damage swing.

entries.name: Harvest
entries.displayTemplate: heal {value}% of max health when you land the killing blow
entries.notes: NEW family minted on this group's reserved `death` stem (naming.v1.json idNamespaces.affixFamilies), word `harvest` — a mechanical description of gaining something from a death, not a theme adjective. There is no `OnKill` trigger (atom-catalog-ssot.md §3: 'No OnKill — killer arrives as actorIsKiller'), so 'when you land the killing blow' is authored as the same `OnDeath` trigger every other family in this file uses, plus `actorIsKiller: true` — the existing OnDeath filter core.v1.json's own counterPressure.conditions registers as leaf `actorIsKiller` (id `actor-is-killer`), placed in `params` the same authoring-level way `when` already sits there (neither key is in AtomKindRegistry's `resource.delta` ParamSchema; both are trigger/condition shorthand the generator resolves into the row's `when_json`, per spec-atom-schema.md's `trigger`+`predicate` shape). This is the wearer-kills mirror of `martyrdom` (wearer-dies, heals allies): same kind, same heal shape, opposite half of the OnDeath perspective split — and distinct from `lifesteal`, which triggers on every hit rather than only a killing one.

entries.name: Glean
entries.displayTemplate: {value}% chance to fire an additional bullet when you land the killing blow
entries.notes: NEW family, stem `death`, word `glean` (to gather what a harvest leaves behind — mechanical, not a flavour adjective). Same `actorIsKiller: true` + `OnDeath` construction as `death-harvest`, applied to `spawn.entity`/`kind: bullet` instead of `resource.delta` — the wearer-kills mirror of `volley` (which fires on every hit) the way `death-harvest` mirrors `lifesteal`, and a genuinely different combination from `summoner` (spawns a zombie on the WEARER's own death, not on a kill the wearer causes).

entries.name: Parting Salvo
entries.displayTemplate: {value}% chance to fire a bullet when this dies
entries.notes: NEW family, stem `death`, word `salvo`. Closes the last open cell in this group's own combination table: the wearer-dies perspective (like `deathblast`/`martyrdom`/`summoner`/`gardener`) crossed with a `spawn.entity`/`kind: bullet` payload (like `volley` on the on-hit side, and like `death-glean` on this side's kill-perspective half) — a slot none of the four shipped families or the two kill-triggered new ones above fill. `powerBand: low` for the same reason every other spawn rider in this file sits there.
